A source of bits from one of R's random number generators

Source: R/rng.R
pract_rng.Rd

pract_rng() tests the generator behind runif(), as chosen by RNGkind(), with its own bits wherever they can be recovered: the 32-bit integers of Mersenne-Twister, Marsaglia-Multicarry, Super-Duper and L'Ecuyer-CMRG, and the 30-bit integers of the Knuth generators, packed into a continuous bit stream. Wichmann-Hill, which adds three fractions, and user-supplied generators are tested on the 32 most significant bits of each number.

Usage

pract_rng(kind = "Mersenne-Twister", seed = 1)

Arguments

kind

The generator, as named by RNGkind().

seed

The seed passed to set.seed().

Value

An object of class zurngtest_source.

Details

The source draws from its own copy of the generator's state, set with RNGkind(kind) and set.seed(seed): the session's .Random.seed and kind are restored after every draw, so testing does not change the random numbers the session draws, and several pract_rng() sources, for example two seeds in pract_interleave(), each keep their own stream.

See also

pract_raw() and pract_fun() for other sources.

Examples

pract_test(pract_rng("Mersenne-Twister"), min_bytes = 2^16, max_bytes = 2^17)
#> PractRand 0.96 test of R's Mersenne-Twister generator (seed 1), its 32-bit integers
#> length= 64 kilobytes (2^16 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 47 test result(s)
#> length= 128 kilobytes (2^17 bytes)
#>   no anomalies in 56 test result(s)
#> No failure, time= 0.3 seconds
